text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a big throughput drop in prod-us-west-2 starting ~09:25 PT. Tokens/s down ~60% across the model pool. :eyes:

sam: Confirmed. Grafana shows a sharp CPU/GPU cycle with many worker restarts. Latency p95 up 3x.

leo: I'm seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on a subset of workers, then the allocator triggers compaction and some processes restart.

ashley: Any noisy tenant spikes? KV-cache eviction rates?

maya: KV eviction spiked right before the drop. Prefetch rate also fell. Looks like small-batch churn + eviction thrash.

infra-bot: Deploy event: compaction-sweep job scheduled at 09:24:58 by infra-ops.

sam: Logs from one host (gpu-23):
```
[09:25:11] ERROR worker: CUDA OOM while allocating 120 MB (alloc failed)
[09:25:11] INFO allocator: triggering compaction sweep (reason=fragmentation, freed=0.0MB)
[09:25:12] WARN kernel-selector: fallback to generic-op due to insufficient contiguous slab
[09:25:14] INFO worker: restarting process (code=OOM, uptime=4m)
```

leo: That kernel fallback is the kicker — we lose fastpath int8 kernels and fall back to slower generic code, throughput tanks. The allocator compaction itself is expensive and triggers page migration.

maya: Batching heuristics also oscillating: because of the restart ripple, we get tiny batches (avg batch size dropped from 6 -> 1.7) which multiplies kernel overhead.

ashley: So chain: noisy eviction -> allocator compaction -> kernel fallback -> tiny batches -> OOM/restarts -> more eviction. A positive feedback loop.

sam: I've temporarily cordoned the noisy tenant (tenant-id=t-9842) off the shared pool and routed its traffic to a dedicated instance. Early numbers show tokens/s recovering on the other hosts.

leo: Quick patch idea: raise contiguous-slab reservation for hot models to avoid fallback, and increase KVCACHE pin threshold to reduce churn. Also bump batching warmup window to avoid tiny-batch mode during unstable periods.

ashley: Can we also disable compaction-sweep jobs while we stabilize? That job seems to coincide with first restarts.

infra-bot: compaction-sweep job marked: PAUSE by sam at 09:28:05.

maya: After pausing compaction-sweep and cordoning tenant, p95 latency down to ~1.3x baseline, tokens/s up ~40% vs trough. Still below baseline though.

sam: Heap/profile snapshot from a restarted worker (attached) shows repeated small allocations pinned across many small slabs. We should consider coalescing small allocations in allocator.

leo: Agreed — long term: allocator should prefer slab compaction with minimal synchronous page migration. Short term: pin hot model to larger slab class to avoid fragmentation and increase kv-cache retention time.

ashley: I'll open a rollback PR for compaction-sweep and a tuning PR for batching warmup. Sam/Leo, can you collaborate on a quick patch to kernel-selector to prefer a cached kernel variant when contiguous memory is marginal?

sam: On it. Also enabling enhanced diagnostics to capture slab utilization heatmaps for the postmortem.

maya: Noted. Action items:
- sam: keep tenant cordoned and follow up on routing metrics (ETA 30m)
- leo: prototype slab-reserve change and kv pin bump (ETA 2h)
- ashley: roll back compaction-sweep / open PR for batching warmup (ETA 1h)
- maya: collect heap + kernel-selector traces and start incident doc (I'll own postmortem)

sre-rotation: I've notified oncall pager and set incident severity to S2.

maya: Great. We'll update in this thread as mitigation progresses. :thumbsup:
